title: Mrs. Vivien Hidary: "Parashat Bo"

chapters.title: Introduction to Parashat Bo
chapters.about: The meaning of Bo and the return of Moshe to Pharaoh

chapters.title: Moshe's staff and the cyclical worldview
chapters.about: Moshe's challenges and the contrast between cyclical nature and verticality

chapters.title: The request to worship Hashem
chapters.about: Moshe's inclusive demand to take the young and old to worship

chapters.title: Integrating youth and wisdom
chapters.about: Bringing youthful dreams and elder wisdom to the service of Hashem

chapters.title: The plagues and the elite
chapters.about: The locust, darkness, and the firstborn as strikes against Egyptian elites

chapters.title: Parashat Hachodesh and the keys of time
chapters.about: The new moon, chiastic structure, and the power to govern time

chapters.title: From ma'amarot to dibrot
chapters.about: The transition from the monologues of creation to the dialogue of the 10 dibrot

summary: Mrs. Hidary explores the themes of Parashat Bo, focusing on the struggle between the cyclical worldview of Pharaoh and the vertical, supernatural path of Moshe. She discusses the significance of the new moon as a moment for the Jewish people to take control of time and integrate their youthful aspirations with the wisdom of their elders. The class also examines the structure of the plagues and the transition from the monologues of creation to the dialogue of the 10 dibrot.
questions: What does the word Bo signify in the context of the parasha?
How does the staff of Moshe represent a vertical connection to Hashem?
Why does the Torah include the details about which crops were destroyed by the hail?
What is the significance of the new moon being designated as the first of the months?
How does the structure of the 10 dibrot differ from the 10 ma'amarot?
